cost_model_summary: Customer wants committed reserved capacity pricing with clear unit economics per token. Proposal built around a base committed pool (8 GPUs equivalent) + 2 burst nodes. Financial assumptions used in our model: peak hours demand 2000 concurrent streams, average request 120 tokens, steady-state utilization 65% across committed pool, burst utilization up to 90% during market open. Using Redwood internal cost assumptions, estimated unit compute cost (tokens generated) = $0.00038/token at 65% util with quantized medium model (13B). If utilization drops to 40% unit cost increases to ~$0.00062/token. Committed discount scenarios modeled: 12-month commit reduces effective unit cost by ~22%; 24-month commit reduces by ~30%. Customer is most sensitive to tail-latency SLA credits and clarity on how batching affects SLOs.
sla_requirements: Latency SLO: 95th percentile token latency < 30ms for streaming flows during market windows
Throughput guarantee: 2k concurrent streaming sessions with average 50 tps aggregate per session during peak

throughput_targets: Design target: 2k concurrent sessions; sustained token throughput target 6M tokens/minute during peak; expected p95 response time budget per request 200ms (for 120 token response).
